title: Iowa HHS — IHAWP community engagement requirements
added: Official State of Iowa Website Agencies A-Z Programs & Services Health & Human Services IHAWP Community Engagement Requirements On this page...

About How to Meet New Requirements Exclusions Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) Resources Back to top About By December 1, 2026, certain Iowa Health and Wellness Plan (IHWAP) members must meet monthly requirements to enroll and maintain coverage.

Back to top How to Meet New Requirements There are several ways to meet these new requirements, including working, participating in an education or work program, completing community service, or combining different activities.

List items for IHAWP Work Requirement Activities You must either: Work at least 80 hours per month, or Earn at least $580 per month based on the federal minimum wage.\ Work can be: Paid work Work in exchange for goods or services (in-kind work) Unpaid work Seasonal workers: Income is averaged over six months.
Enroll in a qualifying job training or work program for 80+ hours per month.
Enrolling in an education program at least half-time meets work requirements.

Education programs include: High school GED program at a community college Community college Vocational and technical school 4-year colleges and universities leading to a bachelor's degree 1-2 year programs leading to a master's or higher-level degree Community service through unpaid work with a structured program completed for the benefit of the community meets work requirement activities.

Examples of community service locations: Schools Humane society Libraries Food banks Park volunteer You can meet the requirement by completing a combination of activities totaling at least 80 hours per month, including: Work Education or training Work programs Community service Back to top Exclusions Some people on the IHAWP program are excluded from these new requirements.

These groups include: American Indians/Alaska Natives Those under 19 or over 64 Individuals who are medically frail or otherwise have special medical needs + NOTE: The state may require medical documentation for the medically frail exclusion.

Pregnant or had a baby in the last 12 months while on Iowa Medicaid Caregivers of children under 14 or someone with a disability Participating in a drug or alcohol treatment program Participants in SNAP or FIP work programs Veterans rated as totally disabled Individuals currently or recently in jail or prison Back to top Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) List items for Community Engagement Requirements FAQ Download a digital or print-friendly (153.32 KB) .pdf version of the FAQ.

If the requirement applies to you, you must spend at least 80 hours each month on one or more of these activities: Work:Work for 80 hours per month or earn at least $580 per month (based on federal minimum wage).\ Income from seasonal work may be averaged over six months.
Job Training:Take part in a qualifying job training or work program for 80 hours per month.
Education:Enrolled in a high school, college, GED, or other career and technical programs at least half-time.
Community Service:Volunteer work for 80 hours per month.
You can combine different activities to reach your 80 hours.
Note: New applicants must meet CER for the month prior to the month of their application.
Current members must meet CER for at least two months since their last Medicaid application or renewal.

Pregnant or had a baby in the last 12 months while on Iowa Medicaid Caregivers of children under 14 or someone with a disability Participating in a drug or alcohol treatment program Participants in SNAP or FIP work programs Veterans rated as totally disabled Individuals currently or recently in jail or prison Update your contact information.
Make sure Iowa HHS has your current information (like address, phone number, and email address) so they can contact you about these eligibility changes.
Check your mail and email.
Iowa HHS will send you a letter or email in the upcoming months if the eligibility changes apply to you.
Keep track of, or gather documents for, any work, volunteer, job training, or school hours you complete each month.
Iowa HHS will contact you when this information is required.

To report a change call 1-877-347-5678 or by emailing [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#e5aca8a6b6a6a58d8d96cb8c8a9284cb828a93) If you want to see whether these requirements apply to you, visit our Self-Service Portal and chat with Ellie, our virtual assistant.

To report a change call 1-877-347-5678 or by emailing [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#632a2e203020230b0b104d0a0c14024d040c15) Participants can meet the community engagement requirements by completing approved volunteer hours.

summary.headline: Updated formatting and added specific details to IHAWP community engagement requirements page.
details: Reorganized content structure with clearer section headers and 'Back to top' links.
Clarified work requirement options to include earning at least $580 per month based on federal minimum wage, in addition to 80 hours of work.
Added specific examples of qualifying education programs (e.g., GED, community college, vocational school, 4-year universities).
Specified examples of qualifying community service locations (schools, humane society, libraries, food banks, park volunteer).
Added detailed FAQ guidance: new applicants must meet requirements for the month prior to application; current members must meet for at least two months since last Medicaid application or renewal.
Included actionable steps for members: update contact information, check mail/email, track hours/gather documents.
Expanded resources section with links to flyers, public resource directory, volunteer opportunities, job help, and member letters (including Spanish).
Added note that state may require medical documentation for medically frail exclusion.
summary.who_is_affected: Certain Iowa Health and Wellness Plan (IHWAP) members who are subject to monthly community engagement requirements to maintain eligibility.
summary.navigator_action: Review updated requirements with members, especially the $580/month income alternative and two-month look-back for current members; assist with tracking hours and updating contact information; direct members to new FAQ PDF and self-service portal.
